title: ID0388415-DC/Si-D/AU-[5nlchV]- Door can't press limit switch
description:
Reported behavior/issue:
Door can't press limit switch
Root cause:
Solution:
On DAMEX Sanctioned List:
Warranty Status: Active
This charger’s front door limit switch is not being activated when the front door is closed. You will see my “quick fix” was to stick a piece of cable tie to the door opposite to the switch finger which adds about 3mm extra travel to the switch.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0388415-DC/Si-D/FR-[5nlchV]- Door can't press limit switch CRM:00645000841
additional_info.body:
Hi All
The switch and bracket are all intact and as they should be. It is as though the white button/finger is either too short or the switch assembly is not far enough forward and therefore there is not enough travel in the button to operate the switch. As a temporary measure I have stuck a piece of plastic on the inside of the door which effectively  adds about 3 to 4mm of travel to the button which solves the problem. It actually needs a little more than 4mm as I noticed the switch lost contact the other day when I lifted the charger with a pallet-jack, the slight twisting of the frame was enough to make it change state.
See attached photos.
Regards
Glen

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0388415-DC/Si-D/FR-[5nlchV]- Door can't press limit switch CRM:00645000841
additional_info.body:
Hey Glen,
Thanks for your response.
The image I sent through shows a door gap which was showing the same symptoms you seem to be experiencing.
There is a door alignment process, but it is not yet documented into a formalised instructions from HQ.
In summary, it would requires 2x people and a low profile jack (to get underneath the door for support).
Making markings of the original location helps, in case the alignment is lost during the adjustment.
On the door where the hinges are mounted, there are slots (image attached) to allow adjustment.
These would need to be loosened and then the door adjusted, to remove the gap you have noticed.
I think it would be worthwhile trying this out while the charger is still in the warehouse and under your control.
While it is possible the crate might be misaligning it, it would be worthwhile to see if you can undertake the process locally first, that way if it is still misaligned when it arrives on site, you are able to assist.
Let me know when you would be able to schedule this in with the low profile jack.
With Kind Regards,
Ferdinand Reisch
Siemens Ltd.
Application Service Engineer
Phone: +61 499 701 794
Email: ferdinand.reisch@siemens.com
www.siemens.com.au/emobility
